$meta.title: The KIMulator this site is written against
$meta.description: The KIM's own emulator, a sibling repository like 6502-EMULATOR and pinned the same way. Separate from emulator.json on purpose: they are two machines, with two embed contracts and two postMessage prefixes, and a file that merged them would let a page reach for a parameter the other one answers to. Carries the release the KIM chapter's frame was written against, and the shape of that contract, so the link checker fails on a parameter this release has never heard of.

sources.authority: The embed contract — the parameter table, the panel names, the pad's key names, the documented frame sizes.

$meta.warning: Hand-authored file. Bumping the version here is what moves the KIM chapter to a new release.

frame.note: There is no raster to double here — a KIM is four panels beside each other, so the size follows `panels`, and this is the contract's figure for all four. It is read as a shape rather than a size: the panels scale to whatever box they are given, so the site gives them the width of its own column and keeps only the proportion. It is the contract's suggestion and not a description of what this site draws: two columns need a box over 700 points wide, over 480 high and not in portrait, and the column here is 688 — so a KIM on these pages shows one panel at a time behind a KIM / TERM / BAY switch at every window size, which is what its chapter describes. The contract said 720x480 until v1.0.7, which sits exactly on the height line and is the reason this number moved.

parameters.note: `rom` and `bin` also have a `64` twin carrying the bytes in the URL itself. There is no `prg`, `cart`, `cf`, `muted`, `persist` or `freq`: every one of those went with hardware a KIM does not carry. An unrecognized parameter is ignored silently by the frame, which is right for a reader's page and wrong for this one, so the link checker spells them out.

splash.note: The machine boots to `--ESC TO START--` and means it — `ESC` is the only key that starts it, from the pad or from the wire, and one press starts both consoles. Nothing else does anything, and anything arriving before that press is discarded rather than held over. An embed that should show a working monitor rather than a waiting one says so, which is the hardware and not a quirk of the frame.
